'''Wojciech Samotij''' (<small>Polish</small>: {{IPAc-pl|'|w|o|j|ć|e|ch|-|s|a|'|m|o|t|i|j}}; born 1983 in [[Wrocław]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Wojciech Samotij |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q11836452 |website=Wikidata |publisher=Wikimedia Foundation |access-date=2026-07-25 |language=en |quote=Date of birth: 1983, Wrocław}}</ref>) is a Polish [[mathematician]] and a [[full professor]] at the School of Mathematical Sciences at the [[Tel Aviv University]]. He is known for his work in [[combinatorics]], [[additive number theory]], [[Ramsey theory]]  and [[graph theory]].<ref name="WS"/>

==Education and career==

He studied at the [[University of Wrocław]] where in 2007 he obtained his Master of Science degrees in mathematics and computer science. He received his PhD in 2011 at [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] on the basis of his dissertation titled ''Extremal Problems In Pseudo-random Graphs And Asymptotic Enumeration'' and written under the supervision of [[József Balogh (mathematician)|József Balogh]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=149337|title=Wojciech Samotij - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref> 

Between 2010 and 2014, he was a fellow of the [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]. Currently, he is an associate professor at [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref name="WS">{{cite web|url=http://www.math.tau.ac.il/~samotij/|title=Wojciech Samotij|access-date=22 April 2020}}</ref> He published his scientific work in such journals as ''Random Structures & Algorithms'', ''[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]'', or ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.tau.ac.il/~samotij/publications.html|title=Wojciech Samotij – publications|access-date=26 September 2021}}</ref>

==Awards==
He received the 2013 [[Kuratowski Prize]] conferred jointly by the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] to young mathematicians under the age of 30. The same year, he won the 2013 [[European Prize in Combinatorics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The European Prize in Combinatorics |url=http://www.eurocomb2013.it/index.php?pg=webshow&id=10 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114020557/http://www.eurocomb2013.it/index.php?pg=webshow&id=10 |archive-date=2013-11-14}}</ref> Samotij is also the recipient of the 2016 [[George Pólya Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/polyacomb.php|title=George Pólya Prize in Combinatorics}}</ref> and the 2022 [[Erdős Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.imu.org.il/erdos-prize |title=Erdős prize |website=imu.org.il |access-date=1 November 2023}}</ref> In 2024 he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research]] jointly with [[József Balogh (mathematician)|József Balogh]] and [[Robert Morris (mathematician)|Robert Morris]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7258 |title=Leroy P. Steele Prize 2024 |access-date=2023-12-01 |archive-date=2023-12-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201145027/http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7258 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
